prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: [val] العربية / עברית · Bidi with numbers (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 4 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "الرمز" · longest unbreakable word 32px · one-line width 32px
  col 2: header "المدينة" · longest unbreakable word 45px · one-line width 45px
  col 3: header "עיר" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 53px
  col 4: header "السكان" · longest unbreakable word 68px · one-line width 68px
  col 5: header "ملاحظات" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 390px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Compare cities identified by code, with Arabic and Hebrew names, population figures, and descriptive notes.","reading":"Read each row from right to left, matching the code and two city names before comparing populations and consulting the notes. Wrapped notes will largely determine row height.","groups":["Columns 2 and 3 give the same kind of information: city names in Arabic and Hebrew.","Columns 1 and 4 contain compact codes and population figures that support quick scanning.","Column 5 contains descriptive notes and can use the vertical space created by wrapping."],"keep_intact":["City codes and population figures","Individual words in city names and notes"],"may_wrap":["Notes at natural word boundaries","Multiword city names where necessary"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [53, 66, 52, 89, 99] · table 360×425px · row heights [36, 176, 83, 129] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [53, 66, 72, 89, 79] · table 360×541px · row heights [36, 199, 106, 199] · column headers wrapped 0/5 · tallest cell 8 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [53, 55, 65, 89, 97] · table 360×472px · row heights [60, 176, 83, 153] · column headers wrapped 1/5 · tallest cell 7 lines · mid-word splits 1

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
